clue.text: Indirect speech? You gab and leg twitches!

indicators.note: twitches are jerky movements, so the preceding words are jumbled about

blocks.note: the four words taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone chatters away while their leg jiggles nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: The twitching leg is itself an example of the answer, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures and posture communicate without words, so they are a kind of speech that is indirect rather than spoken.

clue.text: But incomplete chapters in a blast from the past from this?

definitions.text: a blast from the past from this
definitions.note: the instrument is defined by the sound it makes

indicators.note: incomplete means the word before it is cut short by its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming
C is the abbreviation for chapter, doubled for the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which old horn produced some echo of history.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCCINA was the curved horn of the Roman army, so its call is literally a blast from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The buccina was an ancient Roman brass instrument, sounded in camps for signals, so its notes are old-time trumpet calls.

clue.text: Beauty I'd despoiled without a doubt

indicators.note: something despoiled has been ransacked and left in disorder
without tells us to leave out the small word that follows it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
the letter removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone has ruined a beautiful thing, without any doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a doubt' reads as a stock phrase, but 'without a' is the instruction and 'doubt' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubiety is a formal word for uncertainty or hesitancy, the state of being unsure.

clue.text: Ha-ha! Is this the final attempt?

definitions.text: Ha-ha! Is this the final attempt?

blocks.note: surface reading: mocking laughter at a doomed effort
setter's reading: a ha-ha is a sunken boundary trench at the far edge of a garden, so it is literally the final one of its kind

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at what looks like a desperate final try.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken trench hiding a garden's boundary; being at the edge of the grounds, it can be called the final ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt, made when nothing else remains to try.

clue.text: NCOs with a different skin cover

indicators.note: different asks for the word after it in another form, its letters rearranged
to cover something is to wrap around it, so the rearranged word encloses the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Junior officers are issued different leather covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiks are corporal-equivalent ranks in the Indian and Pakistani armies, so they are non-commissioned officers.

clue.text: Where Linnaeus graduated, engendering endless applause

indicators.note: endless means the following word loses its last letter
engendering means producing something new, so the letters are made into a fresh word

blocks.note: the word with its final letter cut

explanation.surface: A graduation ceremony for the famous botanist brings endless clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: Linnaeus, the Swedish naturalist who devised modern species naming, studied at the university in this Swedish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppsala University in Sweden is where Carl Linnaeus took his studies and later taught botany.

clue.text: Indians seeking guarantee: no support for it, one concludes

indicators.note: no means the item named after it is taken away from the long word
concludes places the numeral at the very end of the build

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming
a golf tee is the peg that holds up the ball
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Native people want assurance but get no backing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed piece is TEE, a golf ball's support; taking it from the end of GUARANTEE leaves GUARAN, and I ends GUARANI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guarani are an Indigenous South American people of Paraguay and neighbouring lands, so they are Indians in the old sense.

clue.text: Never? But plods do - in helicopters!

blocks.note: surface reading: police officers do take to the air in helicopters
setter's reading: plod and pig are slang for police, so airborne police make the impossible saying come true

explanation.surface: A doubter says it can never happen, but police officers fly in helicopters all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: PIGS MIGHT FLY is the scornful phrase for something that will never happen; 'plod' is British slang for the police, as is 'pigs'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said sarcastically to mean something will not happen, so it amounts to a retort of never.

clue.text: So the vixen is with child: and us! He must be a demon in bed!

blocks.clueFragment: So the vixen is with child
blocks.note: a pregnant vixen is carrying a fox cub, so she is in cub
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pregnant fox and the speaker's household point to a nocturnal fiend.
explanation.walkthrough: A vixen is a female fox, and its young are cubs, so 'with child' becomes IN CUB.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend an incubus is a male demon that lies upon sleeping women, so it is a demon found in bed.

clue.text: Climbing mountain road, books a pacemaker for one

indicators.note: climbing means going backwards up the page, so the first pair of words is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: an alp is a high mountain
the M1 motorway, with the 1 written as I
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone hiking up a mountain road arranges a heart device.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; written MI, it is a crossword standby for road.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacemaker is a device surgically placed inside the body, an example of something inserted by surgery.

clue.text: Consider Catherine Howard's position and refuse to testify

blocks.note: first meaning: Catherine Howard was Henry VIII's fifth wife, so to take on her place is to be the fifth
second meaning: invoking the US Fifth Amendment right not to incriminate oneself

explanation.surface: A witness ponders the plight of a doomed Tudor queen and stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII had six wives; Catherine Howard was the fifth, executed in 1542.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the Fifth Amendment, an American witness can decline to answer questions that might incriminate them, called pleading that amendment.

clue.text: Grant society two conclusions

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
two words for a conclusion or extremity, a tip and an end

explanation.surface: A funding body awards two final payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed allowance paid to a student or cleric, a sum awarded like a bursary.

clue.text: Was he a dreadful king, this winged predator?

indicators.note: dreadful means very bad, so the words before it come out in poor order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cruel monarch was a bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea hawk is a bird such as the osprey or skua that hunts on the wing, a predator with wings.

clue.text: One Grand Master unknown in Shelley's "paradise of exiles"

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Mikhail Tal was a Latvian chess grandmaster and world champion
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A chess champion of uncertain identity is placed in a line of Shelley's poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelley, who lived and died there, called this land the paradise of exiles in his poem Julian and Maddalo.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's poem names the Mediterranean peninsula a haven for English expatriates like himself and Byron, hence a refuge country.

clue.text: Bush's former chief chronicler died from it

indicators.note: from it means the letter for died is taken away from the word just before

blocks.note: top means chief or leading
a diarist chronicles daily events
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A US president's former top historian has died of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is political, but 'Bush' is any shrub: the definition is someone who shapes bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A topiarist clips and trains shrubs into ornamental shapes, so a bush is formed by this gardener.

clue.text: Breakdown of Norman Bates's sibling?

blocks.note: Norman Bates is the title killer in Hitchcock's film Psycho; the possessive makes the sibling his
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A query about the mental collapse of the brother or sister of Hitchcock's motel keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Bates is the Psycho of Hitchcock's film, so his sibling is the Psycho's sis: PSYCHO + SIS, with the possessive only linking them.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychosis is a severe mental illness, a loss of touch with reality, so a mental breakdown.

clue.text: Retire to take revenge on pollenosis?

blocks.note: first meaning: go to bed, an informal idiom
second meaning, read literally: strike back at the fever caused by pollen

explanation.surface: A hay fever sufferer wants to go to bed to get back at their allergy.
explanation.walkthrough: Pollenosis is hay fever, so hitting back at it is striking the hay.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the hay is an informal idiom for going to bed, which is what retire means at night.

clue.text: Try, I hear you do, this ancient air raid shelter

indicators.note: I hear tells us the words that follow are to be taken by their spoken sound

blocks.note: to test is to try something out
spoken, the two words run together as a three-letter sound

explanation.surface: An offer to test out a very old bomb shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'air raid' is the rain of arrows and stones that Roman soldiers sheltered from by locking shields overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A testudo was the Roman tortoise formation of interlocked shields, protecting troops from missiles falling from above.

clue.text: Gag Eva, eh?!

blocks.note: surface reading: an exclamation about silencing a woman called Eva
setter's reading, a reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction, throwing its first word upward into disorder, produces these five letters

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the idea of silencing Eva.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer's first word jumbled, with 'up' as the jumbling signal, spells 'Eva, eh'; 'Gag' is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to retch, and to heave up is to vomit or try to, so both describe the stomach's convulsions.

clue.text: Magwich appearing at East End (Poplar)

definitions.note: Poplar is also a district of London's East End

indicators.note: End places the compass letter at the close of the name

blocks.note: Abel Magwitch is the convict in Dickens's Great Expectations
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: The Dickens convict turns up in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: East End and Poplar look like a London address, Poplar being an East End district, but 'Poplar' is the tree definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a tree with silvery leaves, so it is one species of that tree.

clue.text: Her Grace posed naked, in a sorry state

indicators.note: sorry means in a bad way, so the two small words are put into poor order

blocks.note: the Duchess of Alba is the noblewoman said to have posed for Goya's Naked Maja
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A duchess who modelled nude is left in a pitiful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her Grace' is how a duchess is addressed; legend says the Duchess of Alba was the model for Goya's nude painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a sovereign Balkan country, and state is a standard word for a nation.

clue.text: "Some corner of a foreign field that is for ever..." France's in being left without warning

definitions.text: "Some corner of a foreign field that is for ever..."

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for a warning goes around the letter

blocks.note: en is French for in
cave, Latin for beware, was the schoolboy warning that a teacher was coming
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Rupert Brooke's soldier's grave, quoted, then France left behind without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Rupert Brooke's The Soldier, whose next word is 'England': a grave abroad that is forever English territory.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a small territory belonging to one country but surrounded by another, as Brooke imagines a grave abroad being.

clue.text: Where nuclear subs are losing time in the outside track

indicators.note: losing means the letter for the word after it is dropped

blocks.note: on a motorway the outer, overtaking lane is the quick one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Submarines are falling behind in a race on the outside lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Faslane, on the Gare Loch in Scotland, is the Royal Navy base housing Britain's Trident submarines.
explanation.definitionFit: HM Naval Base Clyde at Faslane is home port to Britain's nuclear-armed Trident fleet.

clue.text: Modern style expression of Dadaist

indicators.note: expression is read as pressing out, squeezing letters from inside the words before it

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A contemporary manner as the voice of an avant-garde artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German painter who belonged to the Dada movement before moving into Surrealism.

clue.text: Hello, hello! There's a lot of bacon in the barbecue

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so only the opening part of the word is kept
in places the meat portion inside the pair of greetings

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
the greeting again
the first three of the five letters

explanation.surface: A cheery greeting at a cookout loaded with rashers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hibachi is a small Japanese charcoal grill used for cooking outdoors, a type of barbecue.

clue.text: Solvers resolving Nero's thumbs up!

indicators.note: resolving means breaking down and reworking, so the emperor's name is rearranged

blocks.note: the setter addresses the solvers as you
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Puzzlers working out an emperor's arena verdict of mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Nero's thumb gesture in the Colosseum, but the definition is the modern sense of a thumbs-up as agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the gesture and the phrase signal that a challenge or bet is accepted, a way of saying agreed.

clue.text: Impervious to the fading light

blocks.note: surface reading: dusk, the light dying away at evening
setter's reading: unaffected by the daylight that bleaches colours

explanation.surface: Something unbothered by the dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fading light' suggests dusk, but it means the light that fades things.
explanation.definitionFit: A dye or fabric is described this way when sunlight does not bleach its colour, so it resists bleaching rays.

clue.text: Irritation expressed on behalf of... Who - Mr Townshend?

definitions.text: on behalf of... Who - Mr Townshend?

blocks.note: first meaning: an exasperated exclamation

blocks.clueFragment: on behalf of... Who - Mr Townshend?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: for the benefit of the guitarist of the rock band The Who

explanation.surface: An exasperated outburst, then a question about doing something for a rock star.
explanation.walkthrough: Pete Townshend is the guitarist and songwriter of The Who, so 'Who' is the band, not a question word.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a mild oath voicing exasperation, a minced form of for God's sake.
